Sediment

Rivers carry sediment from mountains to the sea, and the grain size decides how far it travels before it settles on the bed of the channel and stays there for years.

Rivers carry sediment from mountains to the sea, and the size of each grain decides how far it travels before it settles on the bed of the channel.

Floods move the largest stones, while slow water in summer lets fine silt drop out near the banks, which builds the fertile plains that farmers depend on.
